hits.heading: Third normal form
hits.text: Database Systems: Normalization / Third normal form :: Third normal form (3NF) removes transitive dependencies so that non key attributes depend only on the primary key. If A determines B and B determines C, then C depends on A only through B. Example: Student(id, dept, dept_head) violates 3NF because dept_head depends on dept. Split it into Student(id, dept) and Department(dept, dept_head).

hits.heading: First normal form
hits.text: Database Systems: Normalization / First normal form :: First normal form (1NF) requires atomic attribute values: no repeating groups and no nested relations.

hits.heading: Second normal form
hits.text: Database Systems: Normalization / Second normal form :: Second normal form (2NF) removes partial dependencies. A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and every non-key attribute depends on the whole candidate key, not on only part of a composite key.

hits.heading: Coffman conditions
hits.text: Operating Systems: Deadlock Handling / Coffman conditions :: Deadlock requires four conditions at once: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Breaking any one condition prevents deadlock.

hits.heading: Definition
hits.text: Operating Systems: Deadlock Handling / Definition :: A deadlock occurs when a set of processes each hold a resource while waiting for a resource held by another process in the set, so none can proceed.

hits.heading: Safe state
hits.text: Operating Systems: Deadlock Handling / Safe state :: A state is safe if there is an order in which every process can finish using the resources still available plus those released by earlier processes.
